messages:
maya_support: hey — incoming escal from ACME. They called our tool endpoint to resolve a payment but got a 400. They say the autorouter invoked orders.update_delivery instead of payments.capture. trace_id=abc123, customer report attached.

maya_support: their request (redacted):
```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tool/invoke" 
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_***' 
 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
 -d '{"tool_hint":"resolve_payment","payload": {"id": "ord_9y8z","amount_cents": 5000,"tracking_number":"1Z999AA10123456784"}}'
```

maya_support: response we returned: 400 Bad Request, body: "schema mismatch: orders.update_delivery requires delivery_address OR carrier"

jason_eng: thanks. can you paste the full router decision log (trace abc123) and the platform decision metadata?

maya_support: pasted the router line from logs: 
`router_decision: tool=orders.update_delivery confidence=0.63 matched_keys=[id, tracking_number]`

infra_bot: automated note: request_id=rid-9012, model_confidence=0.63, route_fallback=none, kernel=fast-path-v2

lee_oncall: likely fuzzy-match: payload contains `tracking_number` so orders.* signature matched even though intent was payment. Our heuristic currently prioritizes shared 'id' + non-empty string fields.

lee_oncall: short term mitigation: require payments tools to have explicit numeric `amount` or `currency` in schema so they don't get shadowed by order/update signatures. Can we do a hotfix to validate presence of `amount` before routing to payments?

jason_eng: I can repro locally with the exact payload. stack snippet:
```
Router::choose_tool(payload)
  -> matched candidates: [orders.update_delivery, payments.capture]
  -> scores: [0.63, 0.41]
  -> selected: orders.update_delivery
```
I think the main issue is we accept `amount_cents` (snake) and some payment tools expect `amount` numeric. Many callers send amount under different names, so router matches on id + other keys.

jason_eng: proposed quick fix: add required_fields = ["amount","currency"] for payments.capture in the router config and bump its base_priority by +0.5. Will open PR and ship to canary. Patch snippet:
```json
{"tools": {"payments.capture": {"required_fields": ["amount","currency"], "base_priority": 1.5}}}
```

paul_support: customer workaround while we patch: ask ACME to include `"amount":5000` and `"currency":"USD"` in the payload. Or explicitly set `tool_hint": "payments.capture"` if their SDK supports it. I'll send suggested payload and example. :thumbsup:

maya_support: forwarded workaround to customer, they tried adding amount+currency and call succeeded. They asked why tracking_number caused orders.* match.

lee_oncall: that explains it — orders.update_delivery has a loose signature that looks for `tracking_number` and any `id`. We should tighten that signature too.

triage_bot: created ticket INF-4578: "autorouter: signature shadowing leads to wrong tool selection when payload contains tracking_number" assigned=eng-runtime severity=P2 eta=3d link=https://issues.redwood.ai/INF-4578

jason_eng: adding tests in router unit suite to catch signature overlap and a regression test with example payload from ACME. I'll include the hotfix in canary by EOD and a rollback plan.

paul_support: thanks — I'll follow up with customer once canary lands.

maya_support: marking resolved with workaround; will update when PR is live. cc @lee_oncall for postmortem if needed. :white_check_mark:
